## Test tiers — run the cheapest that proves the change

| Cost | Tier | Command | Proves |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `fast` | `node --test test/lego-foundation.test.mjs` | the foundation vocabulary and registry still parse |
| 2 | `contract` | `node --test test/lego-lifecycle.test.mjs test/lego-foundation.test.mjs` | contract versions, compatibility and upgrade rules hold |
| 3 | `boundary` | `npm run lego:arch && npm run lego:arch:selftest && npm run lego:foundation` | no LEGO reached across a boundary |
| 4 | `integration` | `cd apps/n8n-lego && node --test test/*.test.mjs` | the domains still work together in-process |
| 5 | `e2e` | `node tests/e2e/lego-smoke.mjs && node tests/e2e/settings-compat.mjs` | the real editor UI still talks to the backend (CI, needs Chromium) |
| 6 | `full` | `npm run lego:gate` | everything |

## Selection

```
node tools/lego/impact-graph.mjs --changed <file>[,<file>...]
node tools/lego/impact-graph.mjs --plan --target <lego-id> --change "<description>"
```

Escalation is conservative: unowned files, manifest edits, public-surface edits, dependents, blast radius >= 5 and the editor-UI compatibility path all push the tier up. When in doubt it selects `full`.
